uRatioYLoneMax\ at lepton fraction 0.1. We also showed that, for a given axial coupling, the spin of the $\Delta$ reduces its Gamow--Teller strength per particle from 3 to $5/3$.

hep-th.title: Large-$N$ $π^+π^+$ scattering from twisted Eguchi--Kawai reduction
hep-th.author: Claudio Bonanno, Margarita García Pérez, Antonio González-Arroyo, Ken-Ichi Ishikawa, Masanori Okawa, Fernando Romero-López
hep-th.abstract: We present the first computation of the $\pi^+\pi^+$ scattering length in large-$N$ QCD in the 't Hooft limit, $N_{\scriptscriptstyle{\rm f}}/N\to 0$, using the twisted Eguchi--Kawai formulation of the lattice theory. We employ values of $N$ up to 1156 and consider several quark masses and lattice spacings to achieve controlled large-$N$, continuum, and chiral limits. The chiral behavior of the scattering length is compared with next-to-leading-order Chiral Perturbation Theory predictions. Our result for the low-energy coupling describing the sub-leading quark-mass dependence is consistent with existing S-matrix bootstrap bounds. Combining TEK results with previous lattice QCD data obtained using standard methods for $3\le N\le 6$, we are also able to extract sub-leading $\mathcal{O}(1/N)$ corrections to the large-$N$ scattering length.

hep-th.title: Bargmann-invariant witness of the graviton commutator
hep-th.author: Hiroki Matsui
hep-th.abstract: We identify the phase of a Bargmann invariant of two matter-wave interferometers as a quantum gravity signature that cannot be reproduced by any branchwise-definite classical gravitational field. For matter coupled linearly to linearized gravity, the interferometric coherence factorizes exactly into a conservative Newtonian phase, the characteristic functional of the graviton state, and a commutator phase. For Wigner-positive graviton states, the first two are classically reproducible; therefore, decoherence alone cannot certify that gravity is quantized. The Bargmann phase isolates the commutator, which is independent of the graviton state and of all Newtonian interactions and is bounded by which-path decoherence. For gravity, this radiation-reaction effect is sixty orders of magnitude below experimental reach, but trapped-ion analogs can test it at order unity.

hep-th.title: From Specific Heat Bounds to Penrose-like Inequalities: A Unified Thermodynamic Perspective
hep-th.author: Kai-Peng Lu, H. Lu, Run-Qiu Yang
hep-th.abstract: Under explicit and physically motivated assumptions, we identify a local-to-global thermodynamic mechanism that organizes several previously disconnected inequalities on black holes. We first focus on asymptotically flat, static, and spherically-symmetric black holes, and provide a unified thermodynamic perspective on various Penrose-like inequalities. We also discuss the generalizations in asymptotically Schwarzschild anti-de Sitter black holes/branes. In holographic settings, these bounds imply monotonic behavior of normalized thermodynamic quantities in the dual field theory. Notably, one central integrated inequality can be established directly under the NEC in general static planar symmetric asymptotically Schwarzschild anti-de Sitter black branes. Our purpose is not to claim a fully general proof of the proposed local bounds, but to expose a unified structural perspective connecting local thermodynamic constraints to global geometric inequalities. Establishing the local bounds beyond the classes considered here remains an open problem.

hep-th.title: Probing the Collins effect at photon-photon colliders
hep-th.author: Simone Anedda, Carlo Flore, Francesco Murgia, Cristian Pisano
hep-th.abstract: We propose to study the Collins effect in the production of almost back-to-back unpolarized hadrons (mainly charged pions) by looking at their azimuthal distributions around the jet thrust-axis in the process $\gamma\gamma \to h_1h_2X$. The quasi-real photons in the initial state can be emitted either by two scattering leptons or two charged heavy nuclei in ultra-peripheral collisions. We provide numerical estimates for kinematic configurations in principle accessible at the Future Circular Collider and at the planned experiments on ultra-peripheral collisions at the LHC. We find that the corresponding asymmetries can be sizable, even up to around 10-15%. The proposed measurements would thus shed light on the fragmentation mechanism of quarks into hadrons and, in principle, would allow one to distinguish among different existing models for the Collins functions.

hep-th.title: Multipartite dynamics beyond bipartite entanglement equilibration
hep-th.author: Yan Liu, Ya-Wen Sun, Ren-Jie Ying, Jun-Yuan Zeng
hep-th.abstract: Entanglement equilibration need not mark the end of quantum-information dynamics in quantum thermalization. We show that the complete Schmidt spectra of a fixed tripartition can become stationary while its multipartite correlation structure, distinguished by local-unitary invariants, continues to evolve. This separation occurs exactly within a finite window in self-dual kicked-Ising dynamics and asymptotically in Haar-random circuits. We further demonstrate an independently tunable timescale for multipartite dynamics using quantum-error-correcting codes. When coupled to a locally scrambling bath, ordinary entanglement approaches equilibrium through rapid local scrambling, while weak logical--bath coupling drives a slower reorganization of multipartite correlations. These results reveal a deeper distinction than the ordering of equilibration times: bipartite entanglement and multipartite correlation structure can probe distinct physical channels of quantum-information dynamics, rather than merely different stages of the same relaxation process.

hep-th.title: Decoupled asymmetric thin-shell wormholes
hep-th.author: A. López-Hormazábal, Hishan Farfán-Bachiloglu, Kazuharu Bamba, Francisco Tello-Ortiz
hep-th.abstract: We construct reflection-asymmetric thin-shell wormholes by joining a Schwarzschild exterior to its minimal geometric deformation, which shares the same mass and redshift function, so that the asymmetry is carried entirely by the gravitational-decoupling sector. The deformed side is a black hole sourced by a scalar field coupled to nonlinear electrodynamics, in its branch with a real scalar. We show that the total radial null energy of shell and bulk obeys an exact identity and becomes positive for a sufficiently strong deformation. The momentum flux across the shell equals the radial null-energy density of the bulk, and retaining it yields the linear stability condition in closed form. We prove that stability with a conventional shell response requires the bulk to violate the radial null energy condition at the throat; the deformation instead enlarges the stable domain and moves the transition radius inside the photon sphere. For a stationary extension built on Kerr, the junction is solved exactly in the spin, which fixes how the angular momentum is shared between shell and bulk and where the shell behaves as a rotating fluid. A free-precession model provides an estimate of the gravitational-wave signal of the throat.

hep-th.title: Simplifying 2-Bundle Descriptions of Invariants and Local Dynamics
hep-th.author: Ferreira Bastien
hep-th.abstract: A string couples to a two-form gauge potential whose local descriptions need not fit together as a single global form. Principal 2-bundles provide a geometric description of this gluing. However, we recover surface amplitudes and quantum partition functions, as well as local classical field dynamics, without the 2-bundle formalism. For global phases, topological and index invariants, and twisted-sheaf moduli, established equivalences give alternative descriptions through cocycles, bundles, operators, or modules, with the required global compatibility data. For three-dimensional finite gauge theories with cohomological actions, Fourier transformation expresses the partition function as a sum of partition functions of ordinary finite-group gauge theories. An invertible local substitution reduces invariant classical actions for a class of 2-bundle connections represented by finite-dimensional crossed modules to ordinary gauge and tensor dynamics. These finite and local reductions explicitly eliminate field variables. A four-dimensional quadratic example instead admits a direct cochain evaluation even when an ordinary gauge-theory reduction fails. These results therefore do not require the additional 2-bundle presentation.

hep-th.title: Heavy Heisenberg Algebras, Zero Modes and Modularity
hep-th.author: Darlayne Addabbo, Christoph A. Keller
hep-th.abstract: It is known due to a result of Miyamoto that zero mode correlators of weight $1$ vectors of vertex operator algebras are quasi-modular forms, and that their generating series are Jacobi forms. In this article we generalize this to higher weight vectors. We consider weight 2 vectors that generate what we call heavy Heisenberg algebras. We prove that their zero mode correlators are a specific type of quasi-modular forms. As a consequence, they too can be summed up into a generating series with Jacobi-like modular transformation properties. As an application of our results, we sketch an argument that gives the asymptotic behavior of the dimensions of states of our VOAs.

hep-th.title: Discrete theta and the 5d superconformal index
hep-th.author: Oren Bergman, Diego Rodriguez-Gomez, Gabi Zafrir
hep-th.abstract: 5d Yang-Mills theory with an Sp(N) gauge group admits a discrete analog of the theta parameter. We describe the origin of this parameter in N=1 theories from Type I' string theory, and study its effect on the 5d superconformal fixed point theories with an Sp(1)=SU(2) gauge group by computing the superconformal index. Our result confirms the lack of global symmetry enhancement in the so-called \tilde{E}_1 theory.

hep-th.title: Black holes in thermal bath live shorter: Implications for primordial black holes
hep-th.author: Jitumani Kalita, Debaprasad Maity, Ayan Chatterjee
hep-th.abstract: Hawking radiation from a non-extremal black hole is known to be approximately Planckian. The thermal spectrum receives multiple corrections including greybody factors and due to kinematical restrictions on the infrared and ultraviolet frequencies. We show that another significant correction to the spectrum arises if the black hole is assumed to live in a thermal bath and the emitted radiation gets thermalised at the bath temperature. This modification reshapes the thermal spectrum, and leads to appreciable deviation from standard results including modification in the decay rate of black holes. We argue that this altered decay rate has significance for cosmology and, in a realistic setting, show that it alters the life time of primordial black holes (PBHs) in the early universe. In particular, the very light PBHs formed right after the end of inflation decay faster which may have interesting phenomenological implications.

hep-th.title: From the massive Schwinger model to unimodular Euclidean gravity with fermions
hep-th.author: Thales F. Bittencourt, Rodrigo F. Sobreiro
hep-th.abstract: The massive Schwinger model (two-dimensional electrodynamics coupled to Dirac fermions) in Euclidean spacetime is mapped onto two-dimensional unimodular gravity in the first-order formalism, also including fermions. The idea of the map relies almost entirely on the isomorphism between the gauge groups $U(1)$ and $SO(2)$. However, the resulting fermion-gravity coupling differs from the conventional form, explicitly violating parity and time-reversal symmetries. Moreover, these fermions exhibit an unconventional transformation behavior under $SO(2)$ transformations. We show, however, that these properties are absent on the gravitational side of the mapping when starting from an axial massive Schwinger model. Several explicit examples of the mapping are considered, including the constant electric field and point-particle systems. For these examples, we explicitly derive the corresponding gravitational manifolds and compute the associated metrics. Furthermore, we analyze the consistency of the mapping at the quantum level using the path-integral formalism and Becchi-Rouet-Stora-Tyutin (BRST) techniques. Our results demonstrate that the proposed mapping remains consistent at the quantum level, establishing a formal BRST-compatible field correspondence between quantum electrodynamics and quantum gravity, at least at the $U(1) - SO(2)$ gauge sector, which does not include the diffeomorphic features of gravity.

hep-th.title: Holographic Timelike c-function
hep-th.author: Dimitrios Giataganas
hep-th.abstract: The integration of high-energy degrees of freedom along the renormalization group (RG) flow in Poincaré-invariant theories is captured by a monotonic c-function. For such theories, holographic c-functions have been constructed using entanglement entropy. However, in theories with broken Lorentz invariance, these constructions generally fail, reflecting both the violation of entanglement RG monotonicity and its limitations in capturing essential features of nonrelativistic RG flows. Since many quantum many-body systems lack Lorentz invariance, it is important to identify a quantity that captures the decrease of effective degrees of freedom along such flows. We show that the recently introduced holographic timelike entanglement entropy naturally gives rise to a new c-function applicable to all such theories, which moreover obeys a geometric upper bound on its rate of change. We further demonstrate the existence of this c-function in theories with Lifshitz and hyperscaling-violating fixed points, showing that, provided the null energy condition, thermodynamic stability and explicit geometric conditions on the flow are satisfied, it obeys the expected RG monotonicity.

hep-th.title: Charged Black-Hole Binary Evolution at Second Post-Newtonian Order
hep-th.author: Andrea Placidi, Elisa Grilli, Marta Orselli, Matteo Pegorin, Nicola Bartolo, Pierpaolo Mastrolia
hep-th.abstract: We study the dynamics of electrically charged black-hole binaries and their gravitational-wave emission during the inspiral phase. Within the post-Newtonian framework, we derive the conservative and dissipative dynamics up to second order (2PN), combining Effective Field Theory and classical methods. We compute the NNLO conservative Lagrangian, LO dissipative effects in harmonic and Lorenz gauges, and provide the equations of motion, center-of-mass transformations, and the Lagrangian/Hamiltonian in ADM-type coordinates. We also obtain gauge-invariant expressions for the binding energy, periastron advance in quasi-circular orbits, and the scattering angle in unbound orbits. Our results extend previous analyses and are fully consistent with recent post-Minkowskian findings.

hep-th.title: The $Z_N$ equivariant Virasoro algebra via alternative Sugawara constructions
hep-th.author: Armin Ghazi, Ahmad Moradpouri
hep-th.abstract: In this paper, we study the $u(1)^2$ Kac--Moody algebra and generalize the standard Sugawara construction of the Virasoro algebra to an infinite family of new realizations. In this case, in addition to the standard invariant tensor $\delta^{ij}$, there exists another invariant tensor $\epsilon^{ij}$, which enables the construction of genuinely new realizations beyond the conventional one. We show that these new realizations arise from a $\mathbb{Z}_N$-grading of the mode index $n$ of the Virasoro generators $L_n$ and the space of such realizations corresponds to points of a possibly singular algebraic variety. For the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ and $\mathbb{Z}_3$ cases, the space of all such constructions is topologically equivalent to a cylinder, while for $\mathbb{Z}_4$ it forms a non-compact real four-dimensional manifold. We show that the spaces of constructions for $Z_{2N}$ and $Z_{2N+1}$ are closely similar. Furthermore, we reformulate the problem within an action-principle framework by introducing $\mathbb{Z}_N$-equivariant maps, which provide a systematic method for constructing conformal field theories endowed with these generalized Virasoro symmetries. This formulation reproduces the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ case and supports the idea that $\mathbb{Z}_N$-equivariance offers a consistent and unified approach to generating extended conformal algebras. Finally, we analyze the corresponding Virasoro-Kac-Moody-like algebras associated with these constructions and show that they represent nontrivial (up to local field transformations) of the well-known Virasoro-Kac-Moody algebra.

hep-th.title: Timelike Entanglement Entropy and Renormalization Group Flow Irreversibility
hep-th.author: Dimitrios Giataganas
hep-th.abstract: We study holographic $c$-theorems based on timelike entanglement entropy and show that timelike $c$-functions capture irreversible renormalization group (RG) flow. We demonstrate that timelike $c$-functions are applicable to both relativistic and nonrelativistic quantum matter in nematic phases with broken rotational symmetry, and that they remain monotonic along holographic anisotropic RG flows under explicit geometric conditions, thereby passing some of the most stringent consistency tests. We derive the exact flow of the composite timelike $c$-function in general homogeneous anisotropic geometries and establish the $c$-theorem for adiabatic flows. Across all classes of scaling backgrounds examined, consistent with the null energy condition and thermodynamic stability, the monotonicity condition universally reduces to a constraint on a running geometric effective dimension. We further construct a second $c$-function purely from the imaginary part of the timelike entanglement entropy and prove its monotonicity under the local effective-dimension condition, without requiring adiabaticity. For Poincaré-invariant flows, this condition follows directly from the null energy condition. Moreover, we identify a geometric upper bound on the rate of change of the timelike $c$-functions, which constrains how rapidly effective degrees of freedom can be coarse-grained. Our results suggest that capturing RG irreversibility in nonrelativistic flows requires observables that are intrinsically sensitive to the temporal direction. The applicability of holographic $c$-theorems is thus extended to highly nontrivial RG flows and points toward a new information-theoretic diagnostic of holographic RG dynamics.

hep-th.title: The species scale and the refined TCC bounds
hep-th.author: Ahmad. Moradpouri
hep-th.abstract: The species scale $\Lambda_s$, is the energy scale at which quantum corrections to Einstein's theory of gravity become significant. In many cases, this scale corresponds to the string mass scale, or the higher-dimensional Planck scale, which can be much lower than the Planck scale in the weak coupling limit. In this note, we explore two variants of the trans-Planckian censorship conjecture (TCC), which we refer to as the refined TCC conjectures. These versions are related to the species scale as a new cutoff in quantum gravity, and we study whether stringy or quantum modes remain stringy or quantum and never exceed the Hubble horizon. The refined TCCs predict a shorter lifetime for de-Sitter spacetime and impose a bound on the cosmological constant. We also show that one of these conjectures violates some decelerating expansions as opposed to the standard TCC bound. We present supporting evidence for the refined TCCs where its consequences are compatible with other swampland results. The most clear consequence of it is the lower bound for $|\frac{\Lambda'_s}{\Lambda_s}|>\frac{1}{\sqrt{(d-1)(d-2)}}$ which is expected from other swampland criteria. Furthermore, it is argued that both the TCC and the refined TCC are incompatible with the big-bang singularity. Therefore, if the TCC and the refined TCC hold, the big-bang singularity must be ruled out. In scenarios such as string gas cosmology, where the TCC is realized, the spacetime background remains completely regular. In addition to this line of reasoning, we argue for a lower bound on the $\frac{d(1/H)}{dt}$ which excludes the de-Sitter spacetime, which is a regular spacetime.

hep-th.title: Bulk Phase Shift and Singularity
hep-th.author: Yueke Jia, Manuela Kulaxizi
hep-th.abstract: High-energy scattering of a light particle off a black hole at fixed impact parameter is described by an eikonal phase, which encodes the resulting time delay and angular deflection. This bulk phase shift admits a holographic interpretation as of the thermal momentum-space two-point function of a scalar operator in the CFT in the Regge limit. At small impact parameter, the phase shift acquires an imaginary part signaling inelastic scattering, obscuring the interpretation of time delay and deflection which become complex-valued. However, in a holographic CFT these quantities can also be extracted from the so called bulk-cone singularities of the position space thermal correlator. Extending this analysis to small impact parameters, we find that the position-space correlator develops a singularity precisely when a null geodesic reflects off the black hole singularity and reaches the opposite boundary. This provides a more robust identification of bulk time delay and angular deflection through singularities of position-space correlators.

hep-th.title: Perturbative Coulomb branches on $\mathbb{R}^3\times S^1$: the global D-term potential
hep-th.author: Arash Arabi Ardehali, Daniel J. Resnick
hep-th.abstract: We develop a Wilsonian description of perturbative D-terms in 4d $\mathcal N=1$ gauge theories on $\mathbb R^3\times S^1$ with chiral Kaluza--Klein spectra. A closed-form, one-loop-exact coefficient of the auxiliary D fields, including 4d Fayet--Iliopoulos parameters and globally valid throughout the holonomy space, determines the leading holonomy potential away from massless thresholds. We establish uniform weak-coupling control there and match across thresholds by retaining the light fields. Gauge-anomaly cancellation renders the Coulomb-slice vacuum equations affine within each chamber bounded by the thresholds, enabling exact linear analysis of their zero sets and numerical reconstruction through DBSCAN clustering of approximate zeros, LPCA denoising, and RANSAC hyperplane detection. Complementing the rank-one applications of the accompanying Letter, we study flavor-twist dependence in the $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ $\mathcal N=4$ theory, and illustrate the numerical reconstruction in higher-rank R-twisted Argyres--Douglas reductions of interest in the SCFT/VOA correspondence. We also relate the same D-term data to leading stationary-phase equations of supersymmetric partition functions and a decompactification limit of the torus twisted superpotential.

hep-th.title: Twirled Perfect Tensor Networks: Computationally covariant holographic tensor networks
hep-th.author: Gurbir Arora, Matthew Headrick, Albion Lawrence, Martin Sasieta, Brian Swingle, Connor Wolfe
hep-th.abstract: We define a novel class of tensor networks motivated by the Python's Lunch Conjecture (PLC) in local tensor network models of the black hole interior. We start from the observation that, for extended black brane states with short-range correlations, the PLC predicts a complexity that is smaller than the upper bound for generic short-range correlated states. We argue that the PLC makes implicit assumptions about the fine structure of the relevant tensor networks modeling gravity that render them non-generic. We demonstrate this explicitly in random tensor network models of the python's lunch, where the exponential complexity is not generally controlled by the PLC exponent. We trace the difference with the PLC to a lack of "computational covariance" in random tensor networks: while the PLC is motivated by an ability to arbitrarily decompose space into low-complexity units provided certain basic rules are followed, we show that random tensor networks do not generically have this property. We propose another class of tensor networks built from what we call "twirled perfect tensors" that do satisfy the computational covariance property and have a complexity bounded by the PLC value. We still find a discrete limitation from local postselection that appears to be absent in gravity. Moreover, we show that this class of tensor networks combines desirable holographic features of perfect tensor networks and random tensor networks, for example, it obeys a lattice Ryu-Takayanagi formula for arbitrary boundary subregions. Though motivated by holography, these tensor networks provide a flexible framework with potential applications beyond quantum gravity.

hep-th.title: Logarithmic corrections to the entropy of near-extremal black holes in New Massive Gravity
hep-th.author: Lucas Acito, Mariano Chernicoff, Julio Oliva, Cielo Ramirez de Arellano Torres, Matías Sempe
hep-th.abstract: We study the one-loop correction to the entropy of near-extremal black holes in three-dimensional massive gravity at the special point where the theory exhibits a unique maximally symmetric vacuum and non-constant curvature hairy black holes can achieve extremality even in the static case. Focusing on the near-horizon AdS$_2\times S^1$ geometry, we evaluate the contribution of boundary graviton modes that become exact zero modes in the extremal limit. We show that the resulting one-loop partition function generates logarithmic corrections to the semiclassical entropy, providing a new extension to higher-curvature gravity of what has been recently obtained for near-extremal black holes in General Relativity.

hep-th.title: Black hole thermodynamics and KK photon quantum corrections in 2D effective dilaton gravity
hep-th.author: Yoshihiko Abe, Tetsutaro Higaki, Yu Miyauchi
hep-th.abstract: We study black hole thermodynamics using a two-dimensional effective theory obtained by dimensional reduction of four-dimensional Einstein--Maxwell theory. For spherically symmetric charged black holes, the resulting dilaton gravity has a nonlinear potential that reproduces the semiclassical phase structure of four-dimensional AdS black holes, including the Hawking--Page transition and the small/large Reissner--Nordström--AdS black hole transition. This shows that the two-dimensional theory before taking the near-horizon and near-extremal limits captures non-extremal thermodynamics beyond the Jackiw--Teitelboim gravity regime. We also include electromagnetic Kaluza--Klein modes on the internal sphere and integrate them out to derive the one-loop effective dilaton gravity. At leading order in the derivative expansion, these corrections appear as constant shifts in the black hole entropy and in the effective charge parameter of the dilaton potential. Therefore, the semiclassical phase structure is not qualitatively modified within this leading local approximation.

hep-th.title: Gravitational Compton scattering at the fourth post-Minkowskian order
hep-th.author: Giacomo Brunello, Mario Meo, Sid Smith
hep-th.abstract: We compute the classical gravitational Compton amplitude at the fourth post-Minkowskian order, $\mathcal{O}(G^4)$, within the Worldline Quantum Field Theory framework. We derive the associated $N$-matrix element, which provides the gravitational-wave scattering phase shift at the same order. As a nontrivial check, we show that our result agrees with black-hole perturbation theory.

hep-th.title: A discrete series gauge field at the late-time boundary of $dS_4$
hep-th.author: Manizheh Botshekananfard, Elif Büşra Güraksın, Vasileios A. Letsios, Gizem Şengör
hep-th.abstract: We study the free Maxwell field on the planar patch of four-dimensional de Sitter spacetime ($dS_4$). We review its bulk canonical quantization in the Bunch-Davies vacuum, and we give a representation-theoretic viewpoint by studying the transformation properties of single-particle states under infinitesimal dS transformations. By taking the late-time limit, we identify two late-time operators with scaling dimensions $\Delta=1$ (leading) and $\Delta=2$ (subleading). We introduce CFT-inspired inner products invariant under the dS group ($SO(4,1)$) for states created by late-time operators acting on the Bunch-Davies vacuum. We explain how the unitary discrete series representations of $SO(4,1)$ associated with the photon are furnished by both operators, in contrast with the Maxwell field on $AdS$ where the $\Delta=1$ operator corresponds to a non-normalizable mode. We also explain how the corresponding discrete series representations of $SO(4,1)$ split into a direct sum of representations corresponding to two helicities $+1$ and $-1$. This is achieved by taking advantage of the dS invariance of the self-dual and anti-self-dual sectors of the photon field strength. In our outlook, we draw inspiration from a recent proposal for the microscopic description of $dS_4$ higher-spin gravity where conformal gauge fields in 3 dimensions play a central role, and we investigate a possible connection of the $\Delta=1$ late-time operator with a conformal spin-1 gauge field in 3 dimensions.

hep-th.title: Variable-mass sine-Gordon with point defects: integrability, soliton transmission, and quasi-conservation
hep-th.author: A.R. Aguirre, H. Blas, H.F. Callisaya, M.C. de Oliveira
hep-th.abstract: We study integrable variable-mass sine-Gordon model (vmSG) with point defects. Using the Lax and Bäcklund-gauge formulations, we construct type-I and type-II defect matrices, derive the corresponding sewing conditions, and generate the bulk and defect contributions to an infinite hierarchy of conserved charges. The lowest members reduce to the standard sine-Gordon energy and momentum in the homogeneous limit, while for inhomogeneous backgrounds they define integrability-generated energy- and momentum-type quantities. Defect compatibility imposes matching conditions on the variable-mass functions across the defect. An analytical transmission factor $z$ characterizes soliton transmission, topological conversion, and absorption/emission processes. We then deform the type-I sewing conditions by parameters $\alpha$ and $\beta$ and derive the associated defect anomalies. Consistent one-soliton transmission is recovered for $\alpha \beta =1$, whereas for $\alpha \beta \neq 1$ parity-centered kink-kink and kink-antikink transmissions display vanishing lowest order integrated anomalies but no generic vanishing at higher order. Numerical simulations reproduce the integrable transmission/conversion regimes and show that non-integrable defects generate small residual disturbances and lowest order quasi-conserved charges, while quasi-conservation of the higher order charges remains unestablished. These results elucidate how exact defect integrability deforms into charge-dependent quasi-conservation and establish a framework for defect-controlled soliton transport in inhomogeneous media, with potential applications to nonuniform Josephson junctions, magnetic and nonlinear-optical systems, and effective molecular and DNA models.

hep-th.title: Quantum Effects in Supersymmetric Galilean Yang-Mills
hep-th.author: Neil Lambert, Joseph Smith
hep-th.abstract: We study the quantum dynamics of supersymmetric Galilean Yang-Mills (SGYM), with a focus on three dimensions where there is a classical scale symmetry. This is believed to be the worldvolume theory describing D2-branes within type IIA non-relativistic string theory and arises as a non-relativistic limit of maximally supersymmetric (relativistic) Yang-Mills. Unlike the relativistic case, we find that SGYM only admits perturbative dynamical excitations on the Coulomb branch. We show that in three dimensions the classical scale symmetry is broken at one-loop due to logarithmic divergences which cannot be absorbed by renormalization of existing couplings. As such we find that SGYM is non-renormalizable. However, we argue that by including additional marginal deformations the original coupling can be renormalized and rendered asymptotically free. Finally, we propose that three-dimensional SGYM flows to a strongly coupled non-relativistic M2-brane theory.

hep-th.title: The growth of $SO(9)$ super-representations in Type II string theory
hep-th.author: Alessandro Georgoudis, Joseph A. Minahan, Gustav Ström, Athanasios Zoumis
hep-th.abstract: We study the growth of massive $SO(9)$ super-representations in type II and type I string theories. We do this first directly by finding an empirical formula that specifies which representations appear at any level, and then compute the multiplicities from a refined partition function evaluated over finite fields up to level 501 for individual representations, and level 226 for all representations. We then derive asymptotic formulae for the growth of any representation, which are constructed by integrating about the peaks of the refined partition function. Using a Rademacher sum we can find very accurate approximations for the multiplicities of the representations. Unlike the superstring partition function, which only receives contributions from the odd Rademacher terms, the multiplicities for any representation have contributions from both even and odd terms. Finally, we apply the same techniques to the ordinary representations, where a simplified refined partition function allows for better computational speed and simpler expressions for the asymptotic approximations.

hep-th.title: M2 brane in AdS$_4\times S^7/\mathbb Z_k$: 2-loop correction to $\frac{1}{2}$-BPS Wilson loop vs localization in ABJM theory
hep-th.author: M. Beccaria, S.A. Kurlyand, A.A. Tseytlin, J. van Muiden
hep-th.abstract: We study the quantization of an M2 brane wrapping $\mathrm{AdS}_2\times S^1$ inside $\mathrm{AdS}_4\times S^7/\mathbb{Z}_k$, dual to the $\frac{1}{2}$-BPS circular Wilson loop in ABJM theory. The classical action and the one-loop contribution were previously shown to reproduce the gauge-theory localization result. Here we extend the analysis to the two-loop order. In an adapted static and $\kappa$-symmetry gauge the world-volume action contains no cubic interaction vertices, so that the two-loop correction is determined entirely by quartic interactions and is manifestly free of logarithmic UV divergences. We find that the bosonic and fermionic contributions combine into a perfect square $ {\mathscr X}^2$ where ${\mathscr X}$ is a linear combination of the bosonic and fermionic 3d Green's functions and their derivatives. The evaluation of $\mathscr X$ requires fixing the $\mathrm{AdS}_2$ boundary quantization of the massless fermionic modes. With the boundary conditions selected by the preserved supersymmetry, $\mathscr X$ vanishes and hence the complete two-loop correction is found to be zero. This result would not be consistent with identifying the M2-brane loop expansion directly with the large-$N$ expansion of the canonical, fixed-$(N,k)$ localization prediction. Instead, it agrees precisely with the recent proposal that the semiclassical M2-brane partition function should be matched to the gauge-theory grand-canonical ensemble, in which the Wilson loop expectation value is perturbatively one-loop exact. The vanishing of the two-loop correction thus provides a non-trivial test of this grand-canonical identification.

hep-th.title: A local second law for black hole dynamics in the charged large $D$ membrane paradigm
hep-th.author: Supratim Halder, Mangesh Mandlik
hep-th.abstract: The large $D$ membrane paradigm provides a perturbative, non-gravitational description of black hole dynamics. While the local second law of thermodynamics has been established for neutral membranes, the explicit determination of the local entropy production in the charged large $D$ membrane paradigm remains an open problem. In this paper, we compute the subleading-order correction to the divergence of the membrane velocity for a charged black hole in a flat background. Using the non-affine null Raychaudhuri equation and the Einstein-Maxwell equation at the physical event horizon, we relate the horizon expansion to the auxiliary membrane kinematics. We demonstrate that the membrane velocity produces a non-negative divergence at the first non-vanishing order in the membrane worldvolume, which is driven by two quadratic forms: the membrane shear and an additional term arising from the Maxwell field. Using this result, we subsequently construct the corresponding membrane entropy current and establish the non-negativity of its divergence through this order, thereby establishing the local second law for the charged large $D$ membrane paradigm.

hep-th.title: Thermodynamics and mechanical laws of causal-diamond horizons
hep-th.author: Carlos R. Ordóñez, Gustavo Valdivia-Mera
hep-th.abstract: We develop a unified thermodynamic and mechanical framework for causal-diamond horizons in Minkowski spacetime. Euclidean regularity fixes the temperature $T_D=1/(\pi\alpha)$, where $2\alpha$ is the temporal extent of the diamond. The regulated Gibbons-Hawking-York contribution gives $I_D^E=-A_0/(4G)$, with $A_0$ the area of the horizon bifurcation surface, and the vanishing equilibrium geometric energy then yields the entropy-area relation $S_D=A_0/(4G)$. For weak matter perturbations crossing a localized portion of the future horizon, a Raychaudhuri analysis relates the associated Killing-energy flux to the area response, yielding a local physical-process first law at leading order near the bifurcation surface and, for classical matter satisfying the null energy condition, a local second law. Uniform conformal surface gravity establishes the zeroth law, while zero temperature is approached only in the limit $\alpha\to\infty$, in which the finite causal horizon disappears. These results show that a coherent horizon-law structure can arise within a causal diamond, a fundamental building block of the causal structure of Minkowski spacetime. The derivation is explicit in $(2+1)$ dimensions, while the physical results retain the same form for spherical causal diamonds in $d\geq3$.

hep-th.title: Finite-cutoff geometry in double-scaled SYK: SYK deformations, branes and CMC-Krylov complexity
hep-th.author: Sergio E. Aguilar-Gutierrez
hep-th.abstract: We develop a finite-cutoff holographic description of the double-scaled SYK (DSSYK) model. We construct microscopic deformations of Kourkoulou-Maldacena and thermofield-double SYK states whose double-scaling limits reproduce a lower-dimensional analogue of $\text{T}\overline{\text{T}}$ and $\text{T}\overline{\text{T}}+\Lambda_2$ deformations, which we denote $T^2$ and $T^2+\Lambda_1$, respectively. The ensemble-averaged theory describes wormhole states in finite-cutoff sine dilaton gravity, and finite-cutoff anti-de Sitter and de Sitter geometries in the low- and high-energy regimes, respectively. The analysis includes both perturbative and non-perturbative solutions to the energy spectrum flow equation, and the regions behind and beyond the respective horizons. Only the perturbative branch admits physical quantum states. We study how to incorporate end-of-the-world (ETW) branes in the finite cutoff holographic dictionary. The ETW brane leads to an additional boundary theory deformation, which leads to black hole or eternal traversable wormhole geometries depending on the existence of normalizable bound states. We extend the finite cutoff length evaluations for constant mean curvature (CMC) slices, which we interpret as complexity in the boundary theory. We discuss possible extensions with matter. Our results provide a microscopic framework for studying the finite-cutoff boundaries, CMC slices and branes in the holographic dictionary of DSSYK.

hep-th.title: Casimir multiplets suffice: strong generation in $\mathcal{N}=4$ $SU(N)$ SYM
hep-th.author: Yifan He
hep-th.abstract: The Schur sector of four-dimensional $\mathcal N=4$ super Yang$--$Mills theory contains infinitely many protected operators, while the invariant polynomials of a single adjoint scalar are organized by finitely many Casimir degrees. I prove that the small $\mathcal N=4$ short multiplets built from these invariants strongly generate the associated chiral algebra, thereby establishing the $SU(N)$ case of the strong-generation conjecture of Beem et al. For every $N\ge2$, all field components associated with degrees $2,\ldots,N$ suffice, in every conformal weight and every degree of the standard relative quantum BRST cohomology. The proof brings together cyclic trace cohomology, quantum lifting, and an arbitrary-degree quartic$--$odd transport identity. Exact field relations and a finite-rank Newton obstruction exclude every additional lowest space, including non-scalar flavor representations; the required normal-ordering corrections and BRST primitives are derived explicitly. The resulting completeness theorem explains how a finite family of supersymmetric multiplets organizes an unbounded quantum spectrum. Every Schur class is a normal polynomial in their components and derivatives, even when its gauge-theory representative involves fermions and arbitrarily many derivatives. This supplies a uniform set of local inputs for meromorphic operator products, bounds protected state multiplicities before cancellations in an index, and gives an algebraic account of the finite-rank reorganization of protected trace operators.

hep-th.title: Monodromy line defects on the fuzzy sphere
hep-th.author: Jiangyuan Qian
hep-th.abstract: Monodromy line defects are of interest in the defect bootstrap program and are dual to electrically charged objects in dual gauge field descriptions. We investigate the Ising monodromy dCFT using a fuzzy sphere regularization, by imposing the twisted boundary condition in the UV. We obtain defect scaling dimensions $\hat \Delta$ and ratios of defect operator expansion (DOE) coefficients using this method. We extend this machinery to the continuous family of $O(2)$ monodromy defects with twist angle $2\pi\nu$. In both cases, the lowest neutral defect scalar lies above dimension one, providing evidence that the monodromy defect reaches a stable dCFT without additional fine tuning.

hep-th.title: Towards differential expansion for generic representations
hep-th.author: Ya.Kononov, A.Morozov
hep-th.abstract: We report the first results of phenomenological analysis, based on extended set of explicitly calculated colored HOMFLY-PT polynomials in \cite{knotebook}. They concern differential expansion (DE), which separates the dependencies on the knot ${\cal K}$ and the representation $R$. %of colored HOMFLY-PT polynomials. DE is well understood for symmetric and rectangular representations, while for non-rectangular $R$ even the knot-independent basis $Z_R^X$ of DE is not known. We concentrate on two issues: the possible derivation of DE and on improved characteristic of its defect. We discuss how evolution families -- twist knots, double braids and 3-pretzels -- can be used to find DE by a peculiar triangular transformation of evolution coefficients. Once $Z^R_X$ are found for particular family, they are expected to stay basically the same for arbitrary knots -- modulo controllable reductions, characterized by the defect of DE, which puts knots into different universality classes. Contrary to original expectation, these classes appear labeled not by a single number $\delta^{\cal K}$, but by a whole non-decreasing sequence $\{k_j\}$, which is squeezed between two staircases, ${ entier}\!\left(\frac{j-1}{\delta+1}\right)\leq k_j\leq{ entier}\!\left(\frac{j-1}{{\rm deg}\,\Delta}\right)$, where the upper bound involves Alexander polynomial $\Delta(q^2)$ and follows from the continuation of the Melvin--Morton--Rozansky-Kashaev limit to $A=q^{-m}$ with $m>0$, when the limit gives a {\it positive} power of Alexander. The old assumption $\delta+1={\rm deg}\,\Delta$ is oversimplified and fails for 19 non-alternating knots with 11 and 12 crossings. Last, we list the differences of non-rectangularly colored HOMFLY for various mutant pairs to demonstrate their universality (knot-independence) and nice consistency with the spirit of DE.

hep-th.title: Random Euclidean CFT$_2$ from Triangulated dS$_3$ Gravity
hep-th.author: Ji-seong Chae
hep-th.abstract: We propose a random Euclidean CFT description of three-dimensional de Sitter gravity with fixed central charge and primary spectrum but fluctuating OPE coefficients. A normalized four-point coefficient extracted from the complex Liouville cosmological wavefunction matches the analytically continued tetrahedral Virasoro graph amplitude. Its two-copy form gives a non-Gaussian OPE correlation, with a modular $S$ transform relating the corresponding amplitude to fixed-angle Conformal Turaev--Viro theory. The $K_4$ graph also determines a compact hyperbolic core assembled from two generalized tetrahedra, with a pleated genus-three boundary. We reconstruct this core directly from a marked family of real Lorentzian de Sitter spacetimes expanding from a tetrahedral initial graph. Inverse normal flow collapses six future-boundary collars into geodesic cuffs. Initial spacelike arc lengths fix the exterior dihedral angles, while boost holonomies and marked seams determine the edge lengths and face pairings. Semiclassically, the OPE correlation acquires an oscillatory phase governed by hyperbolic volume, whose angle derivatives measure Lorentzian holonomies. As four necks of the future boundary pinch and the remaining bends vanish, its genus-three surface degenerates into two four-punctured spheres joined at four nodes. Sphere-tree sewing extends this relation between geometry and wavefunction coefficients to higher-point channels.

hep-th.title: Inverse KLT kernel of AdS string integrals from the intersection matrix
hep-th.author: Yi-Xiao Tao, Shijie Zhang
hep-th.abstract: We develop a topological and combinatorial interpretation of the Kawai--Lewellen--Tye (KLT) relations for $n$-point AdS string-amplitude building blocks, which are disk integrals with multivariable multiple polylogarithm insertions and sphere integrals with their single-valued counterparts. Building on the framework of twisted de Rham theory over a noncommutative ring, we reformulate the problem in terms of associahedral chambers of the moduli space loaded with solutions of the Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov equation. We construct regularized twisted cycles and express their intersection pairings through local monodromies and Drinfeld associators, which control transport between fusion-tree normalizations. Organizing the intersection contributions by common boundary faces yields the intersection matrix, which is identified with the inverse KLT kernel by the twisted period relation. The field-theory limit of the inverse KLT kernel is also given.

hep-th.title: Six and seven dimensional extrema of Non-SUSY heterotic theory with non-maximal enhancements
hep-th.author: Stevell Muller, Daniel Robbins, Hassaan Saleem
hep-th.abstract: We propose a construction of non-supersymmetric heterotic theories on $T^n$ for $n=1,2,3,4$ which lead to extrema of the one-loop effective potential. In contrast to other approaches, we do not impose maximal gauge enhancement, instead relying on Weyl symmetries of the right-moving part of the momentum lattice to ensure that we get an extremum. The classification depends on finding all lattices within a given genus using Kneser's method. We find several thousand extrema, most of which have non-maximal rank gauge enhancements. Several hundred of our extrema are tachyon-free, and several dozen are also not knife edges. There may be further equivalences among these points, but we find at least 2, 11, and 38 distinct tachyon-free non-knife-edge points for $T^2$, $T^3$, and $T^4$, respectively. In addition, we build on our previous work to study the perturbative stability of $AdS_{3}\times S^{3}\times T^{4}$ backgrounds by checking for Breitenlohner-Freedman (BF) bound violations at the tachyon-free non-knife-edge extrema that we found. The lowest eigenvalues of the Hessian at all such extrema that have a positive one loop potential show violations of the BF bound and satisfy the refined de Sitter conjecture.

hep-th.title: Spin-hydrodynamics in graphene and thermovortical magnetization
hep-th.author: Amaresh Jaiswal
hep-th.abstract: We examine the framework of relativistic spin hydrodynamics in the context of the Dirac quasiparticle fluid in graphene. We develop a spin-hydrodynamic model for a (2+1)-dimensional system of fermions under the condition of small spin polarization. Our analysis confirms that thermal vorticity, which satisfies the global equilibrium condition, is also a solution to the spin-hydrodynamic equations. Additionally, we calculate the magnetization of the system in global equilibrium and introduce a novel phenomenon - thermovortical magnetization - resulting from thermal vorticity, which can be experimentally observed in graphene.

hep-th.title: Factorization in deep inelastic scattering at Björken limit: Reduction to (1+1)D integrable models
hep-th.author: H. Babujian, M. Karowski, A. Sedrakyan
hep-th.abstract: We study the small-$x$ behavior of the proton structure function $F_2(x,Q^2)$ using the combined HERA inclusive deep-inelastic-scattering data and compare it with exact structure functions obtained in integrable quantum field theories. The data are described by a local power law, $F_2(x,Q^2)=A(Q^2)x^{-\gamma(Q^2)}$, where the exponent $\gamma(Q^2)$ increases smoothly with the hard scale. We show that this running exponent is well described by a simple renormalization-group crossover form and is compatible with the illustrative limiting value $C=\gamma(\infty)\simeq0.431$. This reference belongs to the sine-Gordon power-law universality class among the exactly solvable possibilities and corresponds to the coupling $\beta^2/\pi=16/(3-C)\simeq6.23$. The sine-Gordon-constrained fit gives a quantitatively accurate description of the HERA $F_2$ surface, with reduced $\chi^2$ close to unity, and is cross-checked with the overlapping final HERA reduced-cross-section data. These results indicate that the small-$x$ growth observed in deep inelastic scattering is naturally organized by a sine-Gordon-type universality class, while the finite-$Q^2$ dependence is controlled by a smooth crossover toward the corresponding asymptotic exponent.

hep-th.title: On the nature of the black hole information problem
hep-th.author: Thiago T. Bergamaschi
hep-th.abstract: The aim of this work is to present the black hole information problem and discuss the assumptions and hypotheses necessary for its formulation. As the problem arises in the framework of semiclassical gravity, we first review the necessary notions to describe Lorentzian manifolds equipped with physical properties, as well as the physical concepts of the theory that describes the gravitational interaction as the curvature of spacetime, general relativity. From its classical perspective, we develop the formalism to study the dynamical aspects of black holes in spacetimes obeying suitable causality conditions. Equipped with conjectures that nature censors naked singularities and that black holes reach a stationary configuration after they form, the black hole uniqueness theorems allow us to review several relations for the geometrical quantities associated with them. Following considerations of the other fundamental interactions, which are described by quantum field theory, we review the arguments in the formalism of quantum field theory in curved spacetime that give rise to the effective particle creation effect, its approximately thermal character, and the concept of black hole evaporation. With a precise quantification of information in quantum mechanics and assuming that the condition for physically acceptable states is given by the Hadamard condition, we review the result that entanglement between causally complementary regions is an intrinsic feature of quantum field theory. As a consequence, we discuss how the formation and complete evaporation of black holes leads to information loss. Conscious that such a prediction follows if no deviations from the semiclassical picture occur at the Planck scale, we discuss alternatives to this nonunitary dynamical evolution and formulate the black hole information problem. Lastly, we analyze the assumptions and hypotheses that lead to the problem.

hep-th.title: BV Pushforward of Palatini-Cartan gravity
hep-th.author: Giovanni Canepa, Alberto S. Cattaneo
hep-th.abstract: The goal of this note is to show that the standard BV formulation of gravity in the Palatini-Cartan formalism is equivalent, using a BV pushforward, to an AKSZ-like version compatible with BFV data on the boundary.

hep-th.title: Subspace-Protected Topological Phases and Bulk-Boundary Correspondence
hep-th.author: Kenji Shimomura, Ryo Takami, Daichi Nakamura, Masatoshi Sato
hep-th.abstract: While tremendous research has revealed that symmetry enriches topological phases of matter, more general principles that protect topological phases have yet to be explored. In this Letter, we elucidate the roles of subspaces in free-fermionic topological phases. A subspace property for Hamiltonians enables us to define new topological invariants. It results in peculiar topological boundary phenomena, i.e., the emergence of an unpaired zero mode or zero-winding skin modes, characterizing subspace-protected topological phases. We establish and demonstrate the bulk-boundary correspondence in subspace-protected topological phases. We further discuss the interplay of the subspace property and internal symmetries. Toward application, we also propose possible platforms possessing the subspace property.

hep-th.title: Anyonic membranes and Pontryagin statistics
hep-th.author: Yitao Feng, Hanyu Xue, Yuyang Li, Meng Cheng, Ryohei Kobayashi, Po-Shen Hsin, Yu-An Chen
hep-th.abstract: Anyons, unique to two spatial dimensions, underlie extraordinary phenomena such as the fractional quantum Hall effect, but their generalization to higher dimensions has remained elusive. The topology of Eilenberg-MacLane spaces constrains the loop statistics to be only bosonic or fermionic in any dimension. In this work, we introduce the novel anyonic statistics for membrane excitations in four dimensions. Analogous to the $\mathbb{Z}_N$-particle exhibiting $\mathbb{Z}_{N\times \gcd(2,N)}$ anyonic statistics in two dimensions, we show that the $\mathbb{Z}_N$-membrane possesses $\mathbb{Z}_{N\times \gcd(3,N)}$ anyonic statistics in four dimensions. Given unitary volume operators that create membrane excitations on the boundary, we propose an explicit 56-step unitary sequence that detects the membrane statistics. We further analyze the boundary theory of $(5{+}1)$D 1-form $\mathbb{Z}_N$ symmetry-protected topological phases and demonstrate that their domain walls realize all possible anyonic membrane statistics. We then show that the $\mathbb{Z}_3$ subgroup persists in all higher dimensions. In addition to the standard fermionic $\mathbb{Z}_2$ membrane statistics arising from Stiefel-Whitney classes, membranes also exhibit $\mathbb{Z}_3$ statistics associated with Pontryagin classes. We explicitly verify that the 56-step process detects the nontrivial $\mathbb{Z}_3$ statistics in 5, 6, and 7 spatial dimensions. Moreover, in 7 and higher dimensions, the statistics of membrane excitations stabilize to $\mathbb{Z}_{2} \times \mathbb{Z}_{3}$, with the $\mathbb{Z}_3$ sector consistently captured by this process.

hep-th.title: Cosmological and High Energy Physics implications from gravitational-wave background searches in LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA's O1-O4a runs
hep-th.author: TheLIGO Scientific Collaboration, theVirgo Collaboration, theKAGRA Collaboration:A. G. Abac, I. Abouelfettouh, F. Acernese, K. Ackley, C. Adamcewicz, S. Adhicary, D. Adhikari, N. Ball, G. Ballardin, S. W. Ballmer, S. Banagiri, B. Banerjee, D. Bankar, T. M. Baptiste, P. Baral, M. Baratti, J. C. Barayoga, B. C. Barish, D. Barker
hep-th.abstract: We search for gravitational-wave background signals produced by various early Universe processes in the Advanced LIGO O4a dataset, combined with the data from the earlier O1, O2, and O3 (LIGO-Virgo) runs. The absence of detectable signals enables powerful constraints on fundamental physics. We derive gravitational-wave background energy density upper limits from the O1-O4a data to constrain parameters associated with various possible processes in the early Universe: first-order phase transitions, cosmic strings, domain walls, stiff equation of state, axion inflation, second-order scalar perturbations, primordial black hole binaries, and parity violation. In our analyses, the presence of an astrophysical background produced by compact (black hole and neutron star) binary coalescences throughout the Universe is also considered. We address the implications for various cosmological and high energy physics models based on the obtained parameter constraints. We conclude that LIGO-Virgo data already yield significant constraints on numerous early Universe scenarios.

hep-th.title: Impact of a third body on binary neutron star tidal interactions
hep-th.author: Meet Khatri, Ankur Renduchintala, Sayak Datta, Sajal Mukherjee
hep-th.abstract: To model a compact binary coalescence, it is commonly assumed that the binary evolves in isolation. In the present work, we relax this assumption by introducing a distant third body and investigate how the third body would affect the binary evolution. We treat this problem perturbatively and study tidal interaction in the binary due to the third body's presence. We introduce appropriate modifications to the equations governing the orbital motions and the evolution equations of the binary component's quadrupole moment. We compute the radiated energy and accumulated dephasing for the binary. Our findings indicate that for extreme-mass-ratio inspirals, these effects would not be significant. However, for binaries such as intermediate-mass-ratio inspirals, these effects are more relevant, and in some scenarios the accumulated dephasing can reach up to $\mathcal{O}(1)$ radians.

hep-th.title: Web of Non-invertible Dualities for (2+1) Dimensional Models with Subsystem Symmetries
hep-th.author: Avijit Maity, Vikram Tripathi, Andriy H. Nevidomskyy
hep-th.abstract: We extend non-invertible duality concepts from one-dimensional systems to two spatial dimensions by constructing a web of non-invertible dualities for lattice models with subsystem symmetries. For the $\mathbb{Z}_2 \times \mathbb{Z}_2$ subsystem symmetry on the square lattice, we build two complementary dualities: a map that sends spontaneous subsystem symmetry-broken (SSSB) phases to the trivial phase (the analogue of the Kramers-Wannier (KW) duality in 1+1D), and a generalized subsystem Kennedy-Tasaki (KT) transformation that maps SSSB phases to subsystem symmetry-protected topological (SSPT) phases while leaving the trivial phase invariant. These dualities are boundary-sensitive. On open lattices, both subsystem KW and KT transformations act as unitary, invertible operators. In particular, the KT map not only matches the bulk Hamiltonians of the dual phases but also carries the spontaneous ground-state degeneracy of the SSSB phase onto the protected boundary degeneracy of the SSPT phase. On closed manifolds, however, both maps become intrinsically non-unitary and non-invertible when restricted to the original Hilbert space. We demonstrate this non-invertibility via ground-state degeneracy matching (in two copies of the Xu-Moore/Ising-plaquette model), analysis of symmetry-twist sectors mapping, and the fusion algebra of the duality operator. Enlarging the Hilbert space to include twisted sectors allows the subsystem KW map to be formulated as a projective unitary preserving quantum transition probabilities, consistent with generalized Wigner-theorem-based constructions. We also show that the KT map faithfully transmits the algebraic content of bulk and edge invariants diagnosing strong SSPT order: although strictly local SSPT repair operators map to highly nonlocal objects in the dual SSSB phase, the essential commutation algebra and the bulk-edge correspondence remain intact.

hep-th.title: Deep Thermalization and Measurements of Quantum Resources
hep-th.author: Naga Dileep Varikuti, Soumik Bandyopadhyay, Philipp Hauke
hep-th.abstract: Quantum resource theories provide a unified framework for characterizing useful quantum phenomena subject to physical constraints, but are notoriously hard to assess in experimental systems. In this letter, we introduce a unified protocol for quantifying the resource-generating power of arbitrary quantum evolutions applicable to multiple resource theories. It is based on deep thermalization, which has recently gained attention for its role in the emergence of quantum state designs from partial projective measurements. Central to our approach is the use of projected ensembles, recently employed to probe deep thermalization, together with new twirling identities that allow us to directly infer the resource-generating powers of the underlying dynamics. These identities further reveal how resources build up and thermalize in generic quantum circuits. Finally, we show that quantum resources themselves undergo deep thermalization at the subsystem level, offering a complementary and another experimentally accessible route to infer the resource-generating powers. Our work connects deep thermalization to resource quantification, offering a new perspective on the essential role of various resources in generating state designs and on efficient estimation of quantum resources in experiment.

hep-th.title: Can Randomness lead to non-anarchical mixing angles ?
hep-th.author: Aadarsh Singh, Sudhir K Vempati
hep-th.abstract: We study how disorder and graph connectivity affect neutrino masses and mixing in fermionic theory spaces. Extending the construction of Craig and Sutherland, we compare a nearest-neighbour chain, a non-local graph with distance-suppressed links, and a sparse Petersen-type graph, for Dirac and Majorana neutrinos. Strong site disorder suppresses boundary propagation through localisation. When the heavy mass matrix instead has a dominant approximately uniform diagonal, light masses can arise from cancellations in its inverse. A path expansion makes the dependence on graph connectivity explicit. Our benchmark ensembles display broad mixing distributions for some flavour couplings and peaked distributions for others, particularly with weak site disorder and structured flavour input. These observations do not establish a Haar distribution at strong disorder or a statistical preference over neutrino anarchy at weak disorder. The results identify conditions under which disorder can preserve structured mixing, while leaving its quantitative explanatory advantage to a controlled ensemble comparison.

hep-th.title: Elliptic Ruijsenaars-Toda and elliptic Toda chains: classical r-matrix structure and relation to XYZ chain
hep-th.author: D. Murinov, A. Zotov
hep-th.abstract: We discuss the classical elliptic Toda chain introduced by Krichever and the elliptic Ruijsenaars-Toda chain introduced by Adler, Shabat and Suris. It is shown that these models can be obtained as particular cases of the elliptic Ruijsenaars chain. We explain how the classical $r$-matrix structures are derived for these chains. Also, as a by-product, we prove that the elliptic Ruijsenaars-Toda chain is gauge equivalent to discrete Landau-Lifshitz model of XYZ type. The elliptic Toda chain is also gauge equivalent to XYZ chain with special values of the Casimir functions at each site.

hep-th.title: Integrable open elliptic Toda chain with boundaries
hep-th.author: A. Zotov
hep-th.abstract: In this letter we discuss the classical integrable elliptic Toda chain proposed by I. Krichever. Our goal is to construct an open elliptic Toda chain with boundary terms. This is achieved using the factorized form of the Lax matrix and gauge equivalence with the XYZ chain.

hep-th.title: On the existence of toric ALE and ALF gravitational instantons
hep-th.author: Hari K. Kunduri, James Lucietti
hep-th.abstract: We establish existence and uniqueness results for asymptotically locally Euclidean (ALE) and asymptotically locally flat (ALF) gravitational instantons. In particular, we prove the existence of a unique, Ricci-flat, toric ALE and ALF gravitational instanton, for every admissible rod structure, that is smooth up to possible conical singularites. We also give an elementary proof that any toric ALE or ALF self-dual instanton is a multi-Eguchi-Hanson or multi-Taub-NUT solution.

hep-th.title: Towards a consistent perturbation theory at finite temperature
hep-th.author: Passant Ali, Peter Lowdon, Owe Philipsen
hep-th.abstract: The standard approach to perturbation theory for finite-temperature quantum field theories has several issues, including the appearance of ill-defined on-shell contributions in the real-time formulation, and infrared divergences in massless theories. Earlier studies indicate that these issues all stem from the inconsistent thermal generalisation of the Gell-Mann-Low relation, which forms the foundation of perturbation theory in vacuum. This inconsistency arises from the use of free scattering states in the relation, which are known not to exist in interacting thermal theories. In this work, we propose a generalisation of the Gell-Mann-Low relation for scalar theories based on non-perturbative spectral insights, namely that finite-temperature scattering states can be described by damped but stable particle-like excitations, so-called thermoparticles. The perturbative expansion of this generalised relation gives rise to contributions with exactly the same topology as the standard finite-temperature approach, except that now the propagators appearing in this expansion are not those of a free field but of thermoparticles, which depend on the dynamics of the theory. We demonstrate that thermoparticle perturbation theory resolves the known problems of the standard approach. Furthermore, by comparing imaginary-time calculations at two-loop level with numerical lattice simulations of two-point correlation functions in massive $\phi^{4}$ theory, we explicitly show that this framework gives rise to precise predictions, as in the vacuum case, in stark contrast to the standard approach.

hep-th.title: Sensing the Inflationary Production of Scalars
hep-th.author: A. J. Foraci, C. Litos, R. P. Woodard
hep-th.abstract: We review the mechanism by which loops of matter fields contribute to the graviton self-energy during de Sitter inflation. This self-energy is used to quantum-correct the linearized Einstein equations. A Green's function method is employed to obtain exact 1-loop corrections to the plane wave mode functions of gravitational radiation, subject to the usual ambiguity in the initial state. Conformally coupled matter, which does not experience inflationary particle production, makes only a logarithmic enhancement of the rate at which the imaginary part of the mode function goes to zero after horizon crossing. These corrections can be understood, and even summed up, using a variant of the renormalization group. However, massless, minimally coupled scalars, which experience massive inflationary particle production, induce a much stronger enhancement of the rate at which the real part of the mode function approaches a constant. One interpretation of this effect is as a shift of the inflationary Hubble parameter.

hep-th.title: How to Untwist Twisted Gauge Fields
hep-th.author: Serge Lazzarini, Thierry Masson, Louis Usala
hep-th.abstract: This paper provides an isomorphism between the space of twisted gauge fields on a principal bundle $\mathcal{P}(M,H)$ and the space of standard gauge fields on a different principal bundle $\mathcal{Q}(M,G)$ associated to $\mathcal{P}$. This isomorphism extends to local fields on the base manifold, which enables the use of local twisted fields in standard gauge theories (e.g. Yang-Mills-like theories). This allows one to deal with two symmetry groups, coming from $\mathcal{P}$ and $\mathcal{Q}$, respectively. The construction makes use of a larger principal bundle $\mathcal{S}$ which has $\mathcal{P}$ and $\mathcal{Q}$ as quotient bundles. $\mathcal{S}$ is a Hilsum-Skandalis bibundle between the action groupoids $H\ltimes\mathcal{P}$ and $G\ltimes\mathcal{Q}$. The gauge structure on $\mathcal{S}$ encodes both standard and twisted gauge structures on $\mathcal{P}$. In addition, the isomorphism classes of bundles $\mathcal{S}$ up to an isomorphism covering the identity map on $\mathcal{P}$ are in 1:1 correspondence with the equivalence classes of cocycles (up to a coboundary). This paper also provides a new interpretation of (full) dressing fields as dynamic (or active) sections of a principal bundle.

hep-th.title: The left-cut for partial waves in terms of physical amplitudes
hep-th.author: Alexandre Salas-Bernárdez
hep-th.abstract: We derive a novel representation of the partial wave amplitude over the left-hand cut for $2 \to 2$ scattering. We express the left-hand cut of arbitrary isospin and angular momentum partial waves as an integral of right-hand cut imaginary parts. This formulation provides an explicit, exact extraction of the logarithmic branch cut structures, offering a valuable tool to systematically quantify left-hand cut uncertainties in unitarization methods such as the Inverse Amplitude Method or $N/D$ approaches.

hep-th.title: New approach to the estimation of the lowest boundary of an axion mass and axion-electron coupling constant
hep-th.author: Sevinj O. Guseynova, Vali A. Huseynov, Mehriban Sh. Hasanova, Sevinj Y. Rzayeva, Nigar E. Musazade
hep-th.abstract: In this work, we have performed the theoretical estimation of the lowest boundary of an axion mass. We have analyzed the energy spectrum of the electron in a constant homogeneous magnetic field, taking into account its anomalous magnetic moment. We have applied the obtained results on the energy spectrum of the electron in a constant homogeneous magnetic field with allowance for its anomalous magnetic moment to the hydrogen atom electron, which is located in addition to the Coulomb field of the proton, as well as in the magnetic field produced by the magnetic moment of the proton. We have applied the idea of the restriction for the lowest boundary of the axion mass to the triplet-singlet transition between two adjacent levels obtained as a result of the hyperfine structure splitting of the s-levels in the hydrogen atom. We have concluded that the mass of an axion ought to be more than 5.885*10^(-6) eV. We have also obtained the analytical relation for the lowest boundary of the axion-electron coupling constant and numerically estimated its value: the axion-electron coupling constant ought to be more than 1.670*10^(-16).

hep-th.title: Taub-NUT as gravitational dyon with torsion
hep-th.author: Dmitri Gal'tsov, Rostom Karsanov
hep-th.abstract: We show that the Levi-Civita connection for the Taub-NUT metric is singular on Misner strings and generates an Einstein tensor containing the squares of the delta function. This can be improved by introducing torsion, in which case the Einstein tensor may be interpreted as that of a cosmic string with negative variable tension. Komar flows in Misner strings are generated by torsion, which is therefore responsible for the asymptotic Komar charges. The Taub-NUT metric then appears as a soliton supported by two spin-fluid beams.

hep-th.title: A Simple Necessary and Sufficient Condition for Yang--Baxter Integrability
hep-th.author: Mizuki Sanatani, Naoto Shiraishi, Fuga Ishii
hep-th.abstract: Quantum integrability is a cornerstone of the exact theory of interacting quantum spin chains. In its standard formulation, however, one starts from R-matrices satisfying the Yang--Baxter equation, rather than from the Hamiltonian itself. It has therefore remained unclear how Yang--Baxter solvability can be characterized directly at the Hamiltonian level, and how it is related to the existence of local conservation laws. Here we prove that, in a broad standard setting, the Reshetikhin condition is not only necessary but also sufficient for Yang--Baxter integrability, thereby reducing the hidden algebraic structure of integrability to a Hamiltonian-level conservation law. Since the Reshetikhin condition is equivalent to conservation of the total energy current, this Hamiltonian-level criterion is also experimentally accessible. This result establishes a quantum counterpart of the Liouville--Arnold theorem for isotropic spin chains, stating that Yang--Baxter solvability is equivalent to an infinite hierarchy of local conserved quantities. Our result also simplifies substantially the search for integrable spin chains by replacing the search for R-matrices with a direct criterion on local Hamiltonians.

hep-th.title: A different kind of continuum limit for the three-dimensional U(1) gauge theory
hep-th.author: Andreas Athenodorou, Claudio Bonati, Ivan Soler Calero
hep-th.abstract: In three-dimensional compact U(1) lattice gauge theory color confinement can be understood analytically through the dynamics of magnetic monopoles. However, its continuum limit is pathological, since the ratio of the glueball masses to the square root of the string tension vanishes as the continuum limit is approached. We investigate a simple extension of the Wilson action in which the total number of lattice monopoles is coupled to an additional parameter $\mu$. By tuning $\beta$ and $\mu$ simultaneously, we identify a line of constant physics along which the ratio of the lightest glueball mass to the square root of the string tension remains constant. We further show that the same scaling is satisfied, within numerical uncertainties, by the other low-lying glueball masses considered in this work. Along this trajectory, the string tension in lattice units decreases with increasing $\beta$, thus suggesting that the modified lattice action may provide a regularization of three-dimensional compact U(1) gauge theory with a physically well-behaved continuum limit.

hep-th.title: Anomaly in baryon number
hep-th.author: Yutaka Hosotani
